open_points.subject: Missing identities in `store.read_records` calls
open_points.text: “The call also names what a missing identity means … omitted from the answer, `unknown_reference` … or `internal_error` …; a caller never checks the answer for absence itself.”
open_points.question: For each caller and read-by-identity use, which missing-identity disposition must the call name, especially when an identity was obtained through another module or when omission is allowed?
options: Fix a disposition for every call site based on provenance: request-supplied is `unknown_reference`, stored-reference is `internal_error`, and explicitly optional lookup is omission.
Let each public operation’s Errors text determine the disposition, regardless of identity provenance.
Allow each caller to choose any of the three dispositions.
open_points.default_guess: Use provenance-based dispositions and permit omission only at explicitly listed optional lookup call sites.

open_points.subject: Parent-side limit setup failure timing
open_points.text: “the execution is `crashed` (A03 rule 5), and its resources used are the elapsed wall time”
open_points.question: If the wall deadline passes while the parent is attempting to set a limit before bubblewrap starts, is the outcome still unconditionally `crashed`, or does A03’s outcome order make it `timeout`; and from which event to which event is the reported elapsed wall time measured?
options: This branch overrides normal precedence: always `crashed`, with wall time measured from entry to `execute_function` until the setup failure is detected.
Normal precedence still applies, so a passed deadline produces `timeout`; wall time includes setup.
The deadline begins only after all parent-side limits are set, while reported wall time may or may not include setup.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the explicit branch as overriding precedence and measure wall time from entry to `execute_function` until failure detection.

open_points.subject: Runner-side process-limit setup failure resources
open_points.text: “limits from outside (the process count set inside by the runner)” together with “except when the parent could not set a limit before starting bubblewrap … resources used are the elapsed wall time with memory and output both zero”
open_points.question: What `resources_used` values must be returned when the runner cannot set the process-count limit after the environment exists but before user code loads?
options: Report actual setup wall time and peak memory, with output zero.
Apply the parent-failure rule: elapsed wall time with memory and output zero.
Return the ordinary crashed-execution resource measurements.
open_points.default_guess: Return ordinary measured setup wall time and memory with output zero, then confirm environment cleanup normally.
